title: Domino Chain Reaction with Varied Spacing
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D domino chain reaction scene using Three.js. The scene must include physics simulation and a dragon model as a decorative centerpiece.

## Scene Setup
1. Create a Three.js scene with a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 12, 25) looking at the origin.
2. Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (10, 20, 10) with intensity 0.8 and shadow mapping enabled.
3. Create a ground plane (50x50, color #4a7c59) at y=0 with receiveShadow=true.
4. Load the 'DragonAttenuation.glb' model using GLTFLoader from a CDN (use https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.160.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). Scale the dragon to (2,2,2) and position it at (0, 0, -8) as a decorative centerpiece behind the domino chain. Store the dragon mesh reference.
5. Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.

## Domino Chain Setup
1. Create exactly 20 dominoes arranged in a curved path. Each domino is a BoxGeometry(0.4, 2, 1) with MeshStandardMaterial.
2. The dominoes should be arranged along a gentle S-curve path.
3. Implement THREE spacing zones with different gap distances:
   - Zone 1 (dominoes 0-6): spacing = 1.2 units (easy, close together, color #e74c3c red)
   - Zone 2 (dominoes 7-13): spacing = 1.8 units (medium, color #f39c12 orange)
   - Zone 3 (dominoes 14-19): spacing = 2.4 units (hard, wider gaps, color #3498db blue)
4. Each domino starts upright (rotation.x = 0). When falling, rotation.x changes toward Math.PI/2 (or negative depending on direction).

## Physics Simulation
1. Implement a simplified domino physics system (no external physics engine needed). Each domino has properties: { fallen: false, falling: false, rotationProgress: 0, angularVelocity: 0 }.
2. When a domino starts falling, it rotates forward with angular acceleration (gravity-like, ~3.0 rad/s²).
3. A falling domino triggers the next domino when its rotation exceeds a threshold that depends on spacing:
   - Zone 1 threshold: 0.3 radians
   - Zone 2 threshold: 0.5 radians
   - Zone 3 threshold: 0.7 radians
4. A domino is considered fully fallen when rotation >= 1.4 radians. Clamp at 1.5 radians.
5. The chain can potentially FAIL in Zone 3 if the spacing is too wide. Implement a 'difficulty' parameter (default 1.0) that scales the effective reach. At difficulty 1.0, all dominoes should eventually fall. At difficulty > 1.5, Zone 3 dominoes may not reach each other.

## User Interactions
1. A 'Push First Domino' button (id='startBtn') triggers the chain reaction by setting domino[0].falling = true.
2. A 'Reset' button (id='resetBtn') resets all dominoes to upright position and stops the simulation.
3. A difficulty slider (id='difficultySlider', range 0.5 to 2.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) adjusts the difficulty parameter. Higher difficulty = wider effective spacing = harder for chain to complete.
4. Keyboard: pressing 'Space' is equivalent to clicking startBtn. Pressing 'R' is equivalent to resetBtn.
5. Clicking on any individual domino in the scene (via raycasting) should manually push that specific domino (set it to falling), allowing the user to 'help' a stalled chain.

## HUD / UI
1. A top-left HUD panel (id='hudPanel') showing:
   - 'Fallen: X/20' (id='fallenCount')
   - 'Chain Active: Yes/No' (id='chainStatus')
   - 'Current Zone: 1/2/3/Complete' (id='currentZone')
   - 'Difficulty: X.X' (id='difficultyDisplay')
2. Style the HUD with semi-transparent dark background, white text, padding 15px.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- dragonLoaded: boolean (true when GLB model is loaded)
- dominoCount: 20
- fallenCount: number (how many dominoes have fallen >= 1.4 rad)
- fallingCount: number (how many are currently in motion, 0 < rot < 1.4)
- chainActive: boolean (true if any domino is currently falling)
- chainComplete: boolean (true if all 20 dominoes have fallen)
- difficulty: number (current difficulty value)
- simulationRunning: boolean (true after start pressed, false after reset)
- zone1Complete: boolean (dominoes 0-6 all fallen)
- zone2Complete: boolean (dominoes 7-13 all fallen)
- zone3Complete: boolean (dominoes 14-19 all fallen)
- lastFallenIndex: number (-1 if none, otherwise index of last domino that fully fell)
- dominoRotations: array of 20 numbers (current rotation of each domino)
- elapsedTime: number (seconds since chain started, 0 if not started)
- dragonPosition: {x, y, z} (dragon model world position)

## Animation
Use requestAnimationFrame. Update physics each frame with delta time clamped to max 0.05s. The dragon model should slowly rotate (0.3 rad/s around Y axis) as ambient animation.
physics_constraints: Dominoes fall under simplified angular gravity (~3.0 rad/s²). Each domino triggers the next based on rotation threshold that varies by zone spacing. Rotations clamped to [0, 1.5] radians. Chain propagation depends on difficulty parameter scaling effective reach distance. At default difficulty 1.0, all 20 dominoes should complete the chain. Delta time clamped to prevent physics explosion.
